pairs.why: The two are nearly identical, but B's door paint and brass have fainter brushed streaks, which is closer to the smoother finish of the real cards.
A's door shows heavier painterly streaks; B's surfaces are slightly cleaner and smoother, like the real door and gate.
B has less scratchy brushed texture on the plate and door, so it reads closer to the real cards' smooth but not plastic finish.
A's brass has more streaky highlights and its door more grain; B is a bit smoother and more even, like the real cards.
A's door has strong wavy grain strokes, which is the texture the lessons penalize; B's door is calmer and smoother.
A has busier door grain and a glossier, more streaked knob; B's finish is slightly smoother and closer to the real cards.
A's door paint has prominent grain lines; B is slightly smoother, closer to the clean painted door in the reference.
